QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_16

question.text: The SEBI Stewardship Code requires institutional investors (including AIFs investing in listed companies) to do which of the following?

answer.text: Monitor and actively engage with investee companies on performance, strategy, corporate governance, material ESG opportunities/risks and capital structure; also formulate a policy on discharge of stewardship responsibilities.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per SEBI Circulars dated December 24, 2019 and March 30, 2020, AIFs must exercise stewardship responsibilities — monitoring and active engagement on performance, strategy, governance, ESG and capital structure, through discussions, board interactions and voting. Principles are formalised by SEBI. **The Trap:** Avoiding engagement is opposite of stewardship. Divestment is not engagement. SEBI does not vote shares. **Cross-Exam Context:** Same Stewardship Code is tested in XIX-C/D, XXI-B (PMS) and XV (Research Analyst). AIMA for hedge-funds has parallel best-practice guidance, but SEBI Stewardship Code is the statutory baseline in India. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For Cat III activist/event-driven books, publish your voting policy AND the reasoned record of actual votes cast — this not only complies with SEBI stewardship but also anchors your activist thesis in public-record engagement, strengthening post-trade narrative with LPs.
